title: A line or arrow can end at a corner of a box
body:
`line` and `arrow` take `from NAME SIDE` and `to NAME SIDE`, where SIDE is `top`, `bottom`, `left` or `right`. An end given a side meets the middle of that side.

The cloud-search figure shows one DP cell reading the cell above and to its left. The arrow for that read runs diagonally from the bottom-right corner of one box to the top-left corner of the next. With no corner anchors, the figure writes `from 180 126; to 260 186`, worked out from the boxes' positions and sizes. A side's middle would have sent the arrow across the other two cells in the picture.

## Proposal

`from NAME CORNER` and `to NAME CORNER`, with CORNER one of `top-left`, `top-right`, `bottom-left` or `bottom-right`.

## Open

- Whether a point part way along a side, such as `right 0.25`, is worth having too.
close_reason: Landed in 6374cb1 on dev. Ends take top-left, top-right, bottom-left and bottom-right, and follow animated nodes. The note above says how elbow and curve routes leave a corner. The open question about a point part way along a side, such as `right 0.25`, was left undecided and is not built.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/ed2a7ee0
notes.text:
How a route leaves a corner, as built in `6374cb1`:

- A corner end faces out along its diagonal, at 45 degrees whatever the box's shape. A curve's handle runs that way.
- An elbow has to leave along an axis. It picks whichever of the corner's two sides faces the other end more, by comparing the two components of the vector to the other end. From `bottom-right` to an end mostly to the right it leaves right, and to an end mostly below it leaves down. Between two corners that face each other this gives a Z that turns halfway. A corner to a side perpendicular to the chosen axis gives an L.
- On an ellipse the corner is where the diagonal of its box crosses the outline, not the box's corner, which lies off the ellipse.

`connector::square` holds the elbow rule and `build::corner` holds the placement.
